data.title: Chainflip Identifies Vault Attack Entry Point, Says Protocol Won’t Restart Before Security Review
data.description:
Chainflip said its second report on attacks against its Bitcoin and Ethereum vaults identified the attack method, completed a full accounting of losses and covered discussions with all major active liquidity providers. According to Odaily, those providers said they would resume supplying liquidity once the security review and remediation meet requirements and a recapitalization plan is implemented.

The investigation identified validator software for peer-to-peer communications based on ZeroMQ (libzmq) as the attack entry point. It found no evidence linking the attack to flaws in the vault smart contracts, threshold-signature scheme or State Chain logic. Chainflip said the stolen Bitcoin has not moved, while the Ethereum funds deposited into Tornado Cash may also remain unmoved.

data.title: Norse Atlantic Files for Bankruptcy in Europe After Failing to Secure Funding
data.description: According to CNBC, Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy in Europe Friday after failing to secure funding, as soaring fuel costs strained the airline’s operations throughout the year. Its parent company, Norse Atlantic ASA, said the Norwegian carrier no longer had a basis to continue operating and had been unable to secure enough funding to meet its short-term liquidity needs.

data.title: Binance Market Update | Asia Rallies as KOSPI Jumps 4.34% and Hang Seng Tech 6.45%, Bitcoin Reclaims $61K on Short Squeeze as Stocks Rebound
data.description: Asian stocks surged Friday, with the Hang Seng Tech Index up 6.45%, the KOSPI up 4.34% and ChiNext up more than 7%, after China's State Council pledged more market support. US futures also rose, with Nasdaq futures up about 2.4% premarket and SanDisk up 11%. Bitcoin rose 1.8% to about $61,600, though short liquidations (71% of the total) drove much of the move and it still lags stocks. The S&P 500 entered a correction on November 20, but Deutsche Bank says none of the usual bear market triggers is present yet. Short-term bitcoin holders sit on an average 15% loss, a zone that has historically coincided with bottoms.S&P 500 Enters Correction; Bear Markets and Recessions Don't Always FollowThe S&P 500 entered a correction on November 20, its first since April 2025, falling 3.7% to 6,910.39, which is 11.6% below its October 6 closing high of 7,818.93. Eight of the 13 S&P 500 bear markets overlapped with recessions, while five did not. Deutsche Bank's Henry Allen said bear markets since 1962 coincided with at least one of three conditions: a recession, data deterioration that raised recession fears, or a cycle of Fed hikes. He said none is present so far. The November flash composite PMI was 54.6, indicating expansion, and markets are pricing fewer Fed hikes through September 2027 than on October 6.Bitcoin Short-Term Holders Sit on 15% Average Loss as STH MVRV Falls to 0.85, Near July LowShort-term holder MVRV fell to 0.85, almost matching its July low of 0.81 (July 1), per CryptoQuant's Darkfost. It peaked at 1.18 on September 22. A reading below 1 means holders are at an average loss. Darkfost puts the short-term holder cost basis at $71,600, implying about a 15% unrealized loss. He said such levels "have historically coincided with bottom formation" and can offer opportunities for long-term investors.Short Liquidations Hit 71% as Crypto Trails a 4% Weekly Stock Rally; Monero Falls 13% on DelistingsBitcoin rose 1.8% to about $61,600 as US markets reopened for a half-day session, lagging Nasdaq 100 futures (+2.6%). It is up 0.6% this week; holding through Sunday's close would end seven straight weekly losses, the second-longest streak on record. It is still down about 20% in November. The S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Dow are each up about 4% on the week. Liquidations fell 61% to $242M, 71% of them shorts (77% of the $84.7M in bitcoin liquidations), and bitcoin open interest barely changed, which points to short covering. About $7B of bitcoin options expired at 08:00 UTC. Four of the six most traded options were calls; the busiest single contract was the December 25 $50,000 put. Ether options remain defensive, with all six busiest contracts puts. XMR fell 13% after two other exchanges said they will delist it on November 30, citing EU rules on privacy coins; ZEC rose 11%. The CoinDesk 80 rose 1.9%, FET 5.9%, TAO 2.4%. Fear and Greed stood at 11, extreme fear, and the Altcoin Season Index at 63.Hang Seng Tech Jumps 6.45% and KOSPI 4.34% as Chip and AI Stocks Lead Asian RallyThe Hang Seng rose 2.11%, KOSDAQ 8.13%, ChiNext more than 7% and the Nikkei 2.11% to 58,711.11. Zhipu rose 18.57%, MiniMax 17.19% and SMIC more than 16%. The KOSPI closed up 204.47 points at 4,915.68, with foreign investors buying a net ₩1.13T, the most since September 7; SK Hynix rose 6.42% and Samsung 4.55%. Korea's National Pension Service lost about ₩202T in Q3, down 10.8% to ₩1,664T. In China, more than 4,900 stocks rose after the State Council pledged to improve market stabilization, encourage dividends and buybacks, and provide liquidity. Unitree gained as much as 13.66%.SanDisk Jumps 11% and Nvidia 4% Premarket as Memory and Optical Stocks Lead an AI ReboundPremarket (thin volume, may not hold): Nasdaq futures +2.40%, S&P 500 futures +1.79%, Dow futures +1.41%. SanDisk +11.14%, Seagate +7.20%, Western Digital +7.03%, Micron +6.63%, Marvell +7.69%, Nvidia +3.88%. Optical: AXT +10.98%, Applied Optoelectronics +9.26%, Coherent +8.73%, Lumentum +8.38%. Nebius +9.48%, CoreWeave nearly +8%, Anthropic +4.20%. Crypto-linked stocks rose about 5% to 6%. China semiconductor ETFs jumped up to 18%, and the four largest Chinese banks signed more than 600B yuan of buyback loans with listed companies.

data.title: Crypto News | Short Liquidations Hit 71% as Crypto Trails a 4% Weekly Stock Rally; Monero Falls 13% on Delistings
data.description: Bitcoin rose 1.8% since midnight UTC to about $61,600 on Friday, November 27, as US markets reopened for a half-day session after Thanksgiving. Nasdaq 100 futures gained 2.6%, so bitcoin again lagged stocks. It is up 0.6% this week. If that holds through Sunday's close, it would end seven straight weekly losses, the second-longest losing streak on record. Bitcoin is still down about 20% in November, its worst month since June.Stocks and Metals Rally Into the Half-Day SessionAI infrastructure and memory chip stocks led premarket gains, extending Wednesday's advances in global markets. The S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Dow Jones Industrial Average are each up about 4% on the week. Precious metals rebounded: silver rose about 7% to above $44 an ounce, and gold added 2.5% to above $3,670.About $7 billion of bitcoin options expired at 08:00 UTC on the largest crypto options exchange. Traders had positioned defensively ahead of the expiry.Short Liquidations Drive Bitcoin's GainCrypto liquidations fell 61% to $242 million over 24 hours, and 71% of them were short positions, compared with an even split a day earlier. Shorts made up 77% of the $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations. Bitcoin open interest barely changed, which suggests forced short covering, not new leverage, drove much of the rise.Futures trading volume fell 40% to $141.8 billion, while open interest rose 2.1% to $106.1 billion. Traders kept adding positions, but at a slower pace. Funding rates on Binance and other major exchanges cooled to roughly neutral, so long positions are no longer paying a premium. Positioning leans mildly bullish but is not crowded.Options Traders Turn Toward CallsFour of the six most traded bitcoin options over 24 hours were calls, after a day when all six were puts. Three were $62,000 to $64,000 calls expiring November 28 and 29, just above the current price, and one was a $68,000 call expiring December 4. The busiest single contract was the December 25 $50,000 put. Puts still cost more than calls, but the premium has narrowed. Ether options remain defensive: all six of the busiest contracts were puts, led by the January 29 $1,200 put.Privacy Coins Split on Delisting NewsMonero (XMR) fell 13% over 24 hours after two other exchanges said they will delist the token on November 30. They cited upcoming EU rules that bar crypto firms from offering accounts for privacy coins that hide transactions. Zcash (ZEC) rose 11% since midnight, after developers called for moving about $300 million of ZEC out of an older shielded pool. ZEC futures show crowded bullish positioning: longs made up 60% of its $13.5 million in liquidations.Altcoins Keep Pace as AI Tokens RiseAltcoins kept pace with bitcoin. The CoinDesk 80 Index rose 1.9%, and 90 of the tokens in the CoinDesk 100 were higher. DeFi led, with the CoinDesk DeFi Select Index up 4.0%. AI tokens rose with AI stocks: FET climbed 5.9% and TAO 2.4%. CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index stood at 11, in extreme fear, while its Altcoin Season Index rose to 63 from 57.

data.title: Bitcoin News | Bitcoin Nears a Death Cross: After 13 Past Signals, Losses Ranged From 0.3% to 66%
data.description: Bitcoin's short-term price trend is closing in on its long-term trend, setting up a "death cross," a chart signal technical analysts read as bearish. As of November 27, bitcoin's 50-day simple moving average was about 3.45% above its 200-day average, down from a 12% gap a month earlier. After the 13 previous death crosses, bitcoin fell further by a median of about 24%, but the declines ranged from 0.3% to 66%. Bitcoin traded near $61,541.What a Death Cross MeansA death cross forms when the 50-day moving average falls below the 200-day average. It shows that recent prices are weaker than the longer-run trend. The opposite signal, a golden cross, occurs when the 50-day average climbs back above the 200-day, and analysts read it as confirmation of an uptrend.Six Past Signals Preceded Declines of 30% or MoreCoinDesk measured each decline from bitcoin's UTC closing price on the day a death cross was confirmed to the lowest price before the next golden cross. Six signals led to declines of 30% or more. The deepest were 66% after the September 4, 2014 cross, 64% after January 14, 2022, and 59% after September 26, 2011. Three more were between 13% and 19%.Three Signals Were Near-DudsThree death crosses were followed by only shallow declines, leaving traders who sold or shorted on the signal on the wrong side of the market. Bitcoin fell just 0.3% after the September 12, 2023 cross, 2.9% after September 14, 2015, and 5.7% after April 7, 2025.These near-duds all came when bitcoin was already well below its peak, as it is now. But the 2011, 2014 and 2018 crosses also followed steep declines and still led to large further losses. Being far below the peak, on its own, doesn't predict a shallow outcome.For illustration only, a median-sized 24% decline from the current price would put bitcoin near $46,800 (calculated). The historical range is wide enough that the median says little about any single case.

data.title: Brazil’s B3 Pushes Stablecoin Launch to 2027
data.description: Brazil’s stock exchange B3 has pushed the planned launch of its Brazilian real-pegged stablecoin to the first quarter of 2027, after initially targeting a launch this year. According to Cointelegraph, local outlet Valor Econômico reported Friday that B3 is working with six major Brazilian financial institutions—Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Itaú Unibanco, Safra, Santander and XP—on the project. Named Open BRL, the stablecoin is expected to be issued by Banco B3, the exchange’s banking subsidiary, with each token backed by one real; B3 will operate its underlying technology. B3 first announced plans for a stablecoin in December 2025, targeting a launch in 2026. As recently as July, the exchange was reportedly preparing to launch a token called B3RL in the coming months, with infrastructure testing and institutional integration scheduled for August and September. B3RL was designed to be backed by reais and secured by government bonds, facilitating blockchain-based trading of stocks and fixed-income securities starting in 2027. It is unclear whether Open BRL will replace B3RL or operate alongside it. B3 also plans to begin trading tokenized shares in early 2027 using the same order book as conventional equities. In October, executive Humberto Costa reportedly said the platform would initially retain a two-business-day settlement cycle. He also said B3RL would not settle tokenized shares at launch, while round-the-clock trading would require changes to Brazil’s regulatory framework. The country’s Securities and Exchange Commission has been exploring tokenization rules and presented progress from its working group at an industry meeting in October.
